VPNs and Online Privacy

VPN 与网络隐私

OriginalFull translation

[A] Worried about Internet companies spying on your online browsing? You might turn to something called a virtual private network to protect your privacy. But researchers say these networks can themselves be insecure.

[B] Earlier this year, the federal government rolled back rules that would have prevented Internet service providers from tracking your activity online. Comcast, AT&T and other providers are now allowed to track and sell your personal data too—with much less fear of regulatory action.

[C] One solution is a VPN, which is like a dark, secret tunnel you use to go from your computer to a website. While you’re inside the tunnel—clicking on Instagram photos or checking your bank account—third parties can’t see what you’re doing. There are lots of reasons people around the world use VPNs: to hide location, to access work networks, even to avoid government censorship.

[D] Internet providers handle customer privacy in different ways. Some say you have to opt in for them to sell your data. Because of Internet-connected devices, providers can see more than the websites you browse.

[E] So, who cares whether Time Warner Cable or Verizon knows when I turn off my lights or whether I stock my fridge with Swiss or cheddar?

[F] For one thing, those data points can be used to target advertising. And the government or private companies could use the information to deny services, like health insurance—or even water.

[G] Some VPNs promise anonymous browsing for free or just a few dollars a month; they claim not to share your data. But these services don’t always deliver on their promises. Sometimes the medicine might be worse than the illness. In the first major review of VPN providers, what researchers found was alarming. Nearly 40 percent injected malware.

[H] Experts suggest researching a VPN before using it and to think of it as a supplementary tool, not a privacy solution. They advise reading the VPN service provider’s privacy policy to see whether it collects or retains any user information that could be traced back to you.

Full translation

[A] 担心互联网公司窥探你的网上浏览活动？你可能会使用一种叫作虚拟专用网络的工具来保护隐私。但研究人员表示，这些网络本身也可能不安全。

[B] 在本文写作当年的早些时候，美国联邦政府撤销了一些本可阻止互联网服务提供商追踪用户在线活动的规定。康卡斯特、AT&T 等服务商因而可以追踪并出售个人数据，而且对监管措施的顾虑大大减少。

[C] 一种解决办法是使用 VPN。它就像一条从电脑通向网站的隐秘隧道。当你身处隧道之中，点击 Instagram 照片或查看银行账户时，第三方看不到你正在做什么。世界各地的人使用 VPN 的原因很多：隐藏位置、访问工作网络，甚至规避政府审查。

[D] 互联网服务商处理客户隐私的方式各不相同。有些表示，只有用户主动同意，才会出售其数据。由于各种设备联网，服务商所能看到的信息已经不只是用户浏览的网站。

[E] 那么，时代华纳有线或威瑞森知道我什么时候关灯，或者冰箱里放的是瑞士奶酪还是切达奶酪，又有什么关系呢？

[F] 首先，这些数据可以用于定向投放广告。政府或私人公司也可能利用这些信息拒绝提供服务，例如医疗保险，甚至供水。

[G] 有些 VPN 承诺免费或每月只花几美元就能匿名浏览，并声称不会分享用户数据。但这些服务并不总能兑现承诺，有时解决办法带来的问题反而更严重。在首次针对 VPN 服务商的大规模评估中，研究人员发现了令人担忧的情况：近四成会植入恶意软件。

[H] 专家建议在使用 VPN 前先进行调查，仅将其视为辅助工具，不能靠它彻底解决隐私问题。专家还建议阅读服务商的隐私政策，查看它是否收集或保留能够追溯到用户本人的信息。
